_doc: Fire protection read from the documents (Q6497): the fire protection plans of the set and the sprinkler shop drawings among the submittals. Every value carries its source. Symbol sizes are paper sizes (inches on the printed sheet); heights are feet or inches as named.

symbols.source: drafting convention: a sprinkler head is a small circle on the sheet (about 1/16 to 3/16 in across the radius range here), typed by the sheet's own head legend (its symbol beside its description, matched within 20 % of the legend symbol's radius and by its fill: plain, marked inside (hatched or crossed) or solid); with no legend, circles of 0.03-0.1 in radius are taken as heads of no type

bars.source: drafting convention of sprinkler shop drawings: pipe is drawn as filled bars, one bar weight per pipe role (branch lines thinner than cross mains and mains); a bar is at least four times as long as it is wide; bars more than 25 % apart in width are two weights; a size label is lettered within about four text heights of its pipe; a head sits on its branch line (within two head radii)

sizes.source: NFPA 13 (2022) pipe schedule 28.5.2: the smallest branch line pipe is 1 in (steel) and a cross main feeding several branch lines is 2 in or more; used only where neither a label nor a labelled pipe of the same weight gives the size (size_source says so)

heights.source: NFPA 13 (2022) 10.2.6.1 and 11.2.6.1: deflectors 1-12 in below an unobstructed ceiling, a sidewall's 4-6 in below it; trade practice: a pendent's escutcheon at the finished ceiling (0 in), an upright 3 in under the deck, a sidewall at 4 in; the level's ceiling from the documents, else 9 ft

pages.source: company default: up to 64 shop-drawing files of up to 200 pages each, four folders deep; a page is put onto its floor by at least three room numbers it shares with the floor's architectural plan (within 1.5 ft), drawn at a scale between 1/32 in and 1 in to the foot; a head another page draws within 6 in is the same head
